text: Read all three. (1) Spent key with no red line: Key 4's bar was drawn from this phone's own call count, not the key's real balance, so it stayed empty; every spent key is now a full red bar and bars follow the API's own 'left' figure. (2) Chat cut off with the keyboard: the keyboard's height was being added on top of the tab bar's height, squeezing the thread to nothing; fixed. Both go out in the next release. (3) PropLine Pro review (measured on your Pro key from a GitHub runner, one heavy Friday slate, so a snapshot): speed is good, a whole 216-game slate of lines in one call takes 3 s, one game's props 0.3-0.4 s typical (4-6 s worst case; the first run hit timeouts, fixed with a 75 s call and retries). Freshness is mixed: Novig 62 s, Pinnacle 71 s, Hard Rock 72 s, BetMGM 94 s, but FanDuel 4.6 min and DraftKings 5.5 min since last confirmed (their docs say push feeds, the data says polled on this slate). So a fair line from Pinnacle/Novig/BetMGM via PropLine is about 1-1.7 min old, good; FanDuel/DraftKings via PropLine sit at the edge of the 5 min rule and just don't price a bet when stale. Pace: it used about 1,400 requests an hour on day one; now the 25,000 a day is spread over the engine's 17 working hours, props for every game while under 70% of the pace, the +EV sweep under 90%. Verdict: worth it for sharp-book lines, props and the resolved-prop/CLV archive; not a replacement for Pinnacle live feeds. Full numbers: research/propline_speed_freshness_2026-10-16.md. Still to build on it: PropLine results for grading, hit-rate trends, line-movement research (TCL56d).
